newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Petrobras sees possible Iraq talks in H2.
newsitem.headline: Petrobras sees possible Iraq talks in H2.

text.p: Brazilian state oil monopoly Petrobras hopes to restart talks with Iraq in 1997's second half to purchase up to 30,000 barrels of oil per day, a company spokeswoman said.
"Petrobras has an interest in renewing talks with Iraq but nothing has been decided at this point. It is all being studied," said the spokeswoman.
A date for restarting talks with Iraq will depend on Iraq's negotiations with the United Nation's on a price formula, she said.
Petrobras wants a slice of the $2 billion of oil Iraq is allowed to sell over the next six months under the terms of a humanitarian agreement with the United Nations.
"It really depends on the U.N.," the spokeswoman said.
Before Iraq's invasion of Kuwait in 1990, Petrobras bought a peak of 300,000 bpd of Basrah light and Kirkuk crude on a term and spot basis.
"Iraq used to be our main supplier," the spokeswoman said.
